mainEntity.name: Can I patch a hole in drywall myself or should I hire a professional?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor nail holes and small gouges under an inch can usually be fixed with simple spackle and a putty knife. Larger openings, such as doorknob holes or cutouts from plumbing access, require structural backing, drywall tape, and multiple coats of joint compound to stay rigid. A key tradeoff is durability: self-adhesive mesh patches are fast for small fixes, but larger impacts need a solid drywall scrap anchored to framing or backing wood to prevent future cracking. If an area experiences vibration or frequent contact, a properly taped and framed patch is essential.
acceptedAnswer.description: Small holes under an inch are easy DIY projects, but holes larger than a doorknob need structural backing, joint compound, and texture matching best handled by a professional.
